correctness.rationale: The unique graph Laplacian has within-p, within-q, and cross-contrast eigenvalues px+qz (multiplicity p-1), qy+pz (multiplicity q-1), Nz (multiplicity 1). Its pseudoinverse-trace objective is strictly convex on connected feasible weights (positive definite inverse-trace Hessian) and permutation symmetry forces orbitwise equal edges without assuming it. Exact per-unit-price marginal KKT inequalities yield three exhaustive regimes with both sharp thresholds and equality behavior. Closed-form budgets, KKT stationarity, positivity and optimal values are symbolically derived; a standalone reconstruction performed 752 exact rational/symbolic assertions with full independent edgewise Laplacian matrices. Finite checks corroborate but do not replace the all-p,q proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Original framework proves convexity, uniqueness, and KKT criteria, which are correctly credited. Its theorem does not by itself specify where the KKT inequalities switch active sets on two different vertex-orbit dimensions. The new theorem computes their intersections at t_on=2p/(qH) and t_fill=2pN/(2pN-2p-q), proving a nonempty intermediate support phase iff p>q. It does not claim new KKT theory, only this closed classification.

value.rationale: Exact all-parameter solution for a natural community-based resource-allocation model; revealing a nontrivial intermediate regime with no smaller-group internal edges and explicit group-size-dependent boundaries. The middle interval exists exactly under community size imbalance; both thresholds coalesce when groups are equal, and split toward 1 and 2 under increasing imbalance. All conductances and total resistance optima have explicit formulae, allowing reproducible sizing without numerical optimization; no arbitrary finite parameter slice is selected.
